column1: # Published image:tag combinations that are KNOWN to fail verification, with the
# reason and who can fix it. The scheduled catalog-health check reports these
# separately and excludes them from the failure count that opens its issue.
# This file exists so that a permanent, understood condition does not keep an
# alarm open forever. An issue that never closes gets ignored, and then a NEW
# failure hides in it — the exact rot the gap tracker suffered (45% of its open
# issues were already resolved at first audit).
# Two categories, and the distinction matters:
#   superseded  A newer, working tag is published alongside it. The broken tag is
#               kept rather than deleted so anyone pinning it still resolves, but
#               it is not what the catalog offers. Nothing to fix here.
#   upstream    No fix available to us: the defect is in the upstream conda
#               package. Tracked in UPSTREAM.md; the images stay published pending
#               a decision on whether to withdraw them.
# Withdrawn images are NOT listed here — once a repo is deleted there is nothing
# left to verify, and a row for it would go permanently stale. See audit/withdrawn.tsv.
# NOTE this file is the explicit record of an inconsistency we have not resolved:
# the README says "a broken image is worse than an absent one", and the `upstream`
# rows below contradict that. Either withdraw them or accept them deliberately —
# but do not let them sit here unexamined.
# Columns (tab-separated):  repo  tag  category  reason
# Remove a row the moment its cause is fixed; the check will then enforce it again.
# --- superseded: a working tag exists in the same repo ---
anndata
column4: bioconda froze anndata at 0.6.22 (2019); `pandas.core.index` was removed in pandas 2.x so it cannot import. Superseded by 0.13.4--pyhd8ed1ab_0 from conda-forge.

column1: scanpy
column4: bioconda froze scanpy at 1.7.2 (2021); `from anndata import read` no longer exists. Superseded by 1.12.4--pyhd8ed1ab_1 from conda-forge. Reported as aarchbio#63.

column1: transdecoder
column4: upstream build _0 shipped three dangling bin/ symlinks; fixed upstream in bioconda-recipes#69863. Superseded by 6.0.0--pl5321hcbfc158_1.

column1: decoupler
column4: bioconda's newest decoupler IS this broken build (`pandas.core.index` gone). The maintained project moved to conda-forge as decoupler-py; we publish decoupler-py:2.1.6. Different repo name, so not a drop-in replacement for this ref.

column1: # --- upstream: not fixable here, see UPSTREAM.md ---
prokka
column4: bin/real-tbl2asn is x86-64, from tbl2asn-forever 25.7.2f (mislabeled linux-aarch64). Prokka itself works; GenBank submission output does not. bioconda-recipes#69811.

column1: plasmidid
column4: same tbl2asn-forever x86-64 binary as prokka. bioconda-recipes#69811.

column1: maxquant
column4: VERIFIED RUNNABLE: mono is native, `maxquant --help` prints its banner and usage, so the engine works on arm64. What is lost is 5 vendored x86-64 native libs - libbaf2sql_c.so and libtimsdata.so (Bruker BAF/timsTOF raw readers), libxgboost.so, and libSQLite.Interop*.so. Thermo workflows use managed code and are unaffected. Kept deliberately: withdrawing a working proteomics suite over unavailable Bruker input would destroy more than it protects. NOT verified end to end - no search was run. bioconda-recipes#69811.
